claim: For every irreducible \(F(x)=x^6+a x^m+b\in\mathbb Z[x]\) with \(m\in\{2,4\}\), \(9\mid a\), and \(b\equiv1\pmod9\), if \(K=\mathbb Q(\theta)\) for a root \(\theta\), then \(\nu_3([\mathcal O_K:\mathbb Z[\theta]])=2\).

correctness.rationale: For m=2 and m=4 the displayed phi-expansions are exact. With phi=x^2+1, the reduction is phi-bar cubed; the phi-Newton polygon has exactly one positive lattice point on or below it, (1,1), and all principal residual polynomials are linear and squarefree. Ore equality therefore gives nu_3([O_K:Z[theta]])=deg(phi)=2, including the case where the constant phi-coefficient vanishes.

value.rationale: The exact 3-adic valuation of the defining root’s order index is a natural invariant in explicit power-integral-basis problems. The result resolves the even-exponent sextic branch m=2,4 in the b congruent to 1 modulo 9 boundary case and distinguishes failure of this root to generate the full ring of integers from the separate question of field monogenity.
